summary: Platform company (SaaS) for multi-channel contact centers. Evaluating Redwood for a hybrid deployment: dedicated GPUs for peak windows + private control plane for sensitive EU/NA customers. Primary goal: reliable agent assist and ticket summarization with deterministic citations and freshness guarantees.
notes:
- 2025-09-03: Intro call (Jordan/Kim) — high-level fit. Familiar with Redwood from benchmark thread; wants production-grade latency and cost guidance.
- 2025-09-17: Demo — showed agent-assist flow + tool-calling. LumenArc liked streaming and function-calling example.
- 2025-09-29: Security review kickoff — sent SOC2 + KMS questions; asked about audit log retention and search indexing policies.
- 2025-10-01: Technical deep-dive (Priya + infra team). Discussed RAG architecture: connector strategy for support KBs (Zendesk, Confluence, S3), multi-source canonicalization, citation surface, and freshness windows (near-real-time delta updates).
- SE notes: Must support high-concurrency spikes (holiday promo spikes). Target p95 end-to-end agent assist latency <= 350ms for short-context lookups, and batching for long-form summarization without user-facing delay.
- CTO quote: "We can't tolerate hallucinated citations — need provenance and TTL on sources."
- POC ask: ingest 6 months of ticket history (~12M messages), 3 knowledge sources (Zendesk + Confluence + S3 blobs), run 7-day stress test with traffic bursts to 3x baseline. Provide cost/latency profiling across quantized models + fallback policy.
- Legal: data residency rule — EU customers' transcripts cannot leave region. They want a VPC/private CP option for EU tenancy.
- Sales: mid-market pricing acceptable; primary procurement question is whether Dedicated + Private combo required or Dedicated with regional routing solves residency.
- Next steps: share POC ingestion checklist, sample infra diagram for VPC peering, propose initial model variants and quantization plan.
- Short-term win: deploy Redwood Optimize suggestions on caching and prefix-KV to reduce token costs on frequent KB lookups.
- Long-term: integrate Redwood rollouts for canarying new model versions and automatic fallback to cheaper model when under load.

CRM snippets/fragments: "needs deterministic citations", "3x holiday spike resilience", "SSO + audit logs must be visible in console", "prefer single-tenant VPC for EU customers".
timeline:
- 2025-09-03: inbound lead via content benchmark.
- 2025-09-10: discovery call with product.
- 2025-09-17: platform demo.
- 2025-09-29: security questionnaire sent.
- 2025-10-01: POC scoping doc agreed; ingestion samples scheduled.
- 2025-10-06: Redwood to deliver POC plan and SOW draft.
requirements:
- Workloads: agent assist (low-latency retrieval + short generated replies), ticket summarization (batch/async), tool-calling from assistant for internal CRM actions.
- RAG specifics: must support multi-source retrieval with citation per snippet, pinned authoritative sources, freshness window < 10 minutes for KB deltas, ability to invalidate caches on manual content updates.
- Reliability: autoscaling for 3x traffic bursts, SLA for p99 request completion, graceful fallback to smaller models and cached answers.
- Security/compliance: SSO/SAML, SOC2 attestation, per-request audit logs, KMS integration for keys, EU data residency for EU tenants.
- Observability: per-query token cost breakdown, latency histograms, per-model error and hallucination alerts.
decision_criteria: 1) Proven RAG with citation fidelity and freshness; 2) Clear path to meet EU data residency and VPC constraints; 3) Predictable cost under spikes (autoscale + fallback); 4) Ops tooling: rollouts, tracing, and token-level cost breakdowns; 5) Support responsiveness during POC.
next_steps_detail:
- Redwood team to provide POC ingestion instructions and sample connectors (Zendesk/Confluence/S3).
- Run ingestion dry-run w/ 1M tickets by 2025-10-15.
- 7-day load test target window: 2025-11-02 -> 2025-11-09.
- Post-POC: procurement + legal to align on VPC SOW and SLA addendum.
